Dorival Junior's side had previously suffered a 3-2 defeat to Bahia before drawing 1-1 with Mirassol, meaning they have managed just two victories in their last seven matches.

Sao Paulo have won 12 and lost 14 of their 34 league fixtures this season, scoring 39 goals and conceding the same number, suggesting that any progress on last season has been marginal, at best.

Their home form has been considerably stronger, with 10 victories and four draws from 17 matches, while they have conceded just 13 goals on their own turf.

Fluminense, in contrast, have maintained a similar level of performance to last season, although they have an excellent opportunity to climb into third place with just four games remaining.

While they have not been particularly convincing on the road, Flu have managed only four away victories all season, suffering seven defeats and conceding 25 goals.

After losing three consecutive matches, Fluminense have shown signs of recovery in recent weeks, claiming victories over the likes of Internacional and Vitoria.

They have also enjoyed the upper hand in their previous two meetings with Sao Paulo, winning both comprehensively, including a resounding 6-0 triumph in November 2025.

Junior will be without Luciano, Ferreirinha and Newton, with all three players suspended for this encounter.

Right-back Aurelio Buta has undergone surgery on his right knee to repair a meniscus injury and will play no further part this season.

Sabino has also undergone surgery to address a knee cartilage problem after recently suffering an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

For Fluminense, John Kennedy remains a long-term absentee, while Alisson and Matheus Martinelli are also on the treatment table.

Martinelli and Wesley Nata have returned to training, with the former in the final stages of his recovery after resuming ball work last week.

Fluminense possible starting lineup:.

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their new head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

It has been revealed that frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington noted the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington mentioned: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'.

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Sources indicate that pfannenstiel mentioned: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager.

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'.

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

In a recent development, as a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick mentioned: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'.

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

Should Barrott pick up an injury, Kavanagh would be the one to replace him, and that would be quite a lot to handle for the official.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett has warned Howard Webb over how he is right now deciding referee appointments for matches.

"There appears to be very little thought applied to the appointment of match officials to Premier League games," he remarked.

"Referee Chris Kavanagh will be the man in the middle for the Newcastle United vs Arsenal on Saturday, 21 November, with a 17.30 kick off.

"But if Samuel Barrott sustains an injury, then Kavanagh will take over from Barrott, who will be doing his third game in the middle of Anfield this season.

It has been revealed that "Let's hope that Kavanagh does not have to take over. The fact is we would not expect a professional football to be involved in two games over on weekend. Why are we asking our referees to do this?

Webb has plenty of talented officials at his disposal, but he clearly has his favourites in the Premier League this season.

As well as the Premier League, Kavanagh was in action during the international break, refereeing the game between France and Turkey.

Wanting to fix the problem, Hackett suggested: "ProRef need to take advantage of the increased pool of officials available to them after the summer merger of Premier League and Championship officials.".

Tech Report: Chinese scientist sacked after child died in gene-editing trial

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, chinese authorities have sacked the researcher who led an experimental gene-editing trial that resulted in the death of a child.
  • Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.
  • Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: Victor Habbick Visions/SPL.

In a recent development, chinese authorities have sacked the researcher who led an experimental gene-editing trial that resulted in the death of a child. An investigation into the trial by the Shanghai municipal government found that the researcher and his team failed to follow regulations and overlooked warning signs in a safety report. Several others involved in the case have also been punished.

Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.

Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.

It has been revealed that in July, the journal Science and the website Retraction Watch jointly reported that Zilong Qiu, a neuroscientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, led a team that developed an experimental gene-editing therapy for a six-year-old girl with a rare neurodevelopmental disorder called Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome. The therapy was carried by a viral vector that was injected into the girl’s spine and then travelled to her brain. The girl died of medical complications after receiving the therapy at Xinhua Hospital, also in Shanghai, in March 2025.

In a recent development, the institutions involved in the trial — Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine and Xinhua Hospital — have also been reprimanded and instructed to examine their own practices. “I expect the action to send a major warning to research institutes and hospitals across the country,” says Jiayou Shi, a lawyer at the National Research Center for Civil and Commercial Law at Renmin University of China in Beijing.

In a recent development, the trial was conducted under China’s fast-track pathway, called investigator-initiated trials (IITs). IITs allow researchers and biotech companies to test therapies swiftly in hospitals without supervision from the country’s regulators. The Chinese government increased oversight of these trials in May, which Shi states should prevent similar cases in future.

Industry observers note that lizzi Lee, who studies China’s economic and technological policies at the Asia Society Policy Institute, a think tank in Latest York City, notes the trial is “a cautionary tale” for the country’s rapidly growing biotechnology industry. There is real momentum in the industry in China, but clinical oversight hasn’t always kept pace, Lee says. “The investigation is quite candid about what went wrong,” adds Lee.

According to a statement released through China’s state-run media on 13 November, the Shanghai government’s investigation found that Qiu was the main person responsible for the research. He has been sacked from his position as the deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institution, which is affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine. Another member of Qiu’s team, a deputy researcher at Xinhua Hospital, has also been dismissed. Both researchers have been barred from leading or participating in science projects for five years and have been added to a national database of people and organizations that have committed serious breaches of research integrity.

About a month before the girl received the experimental therapy, Qiu’s team received results from a preclinical toxicology study showing that monkeys sustained liver damage, according to Science and Retraction Watch. Investigators found that Qiu’s team failed to inform the researcher in charge of the clinical research at Xinhua Hospital in a timely fashion about the results of the primate experiment, which meant “the early warning signal” in the safety report was not “given high attention”, according to the statement. The clinical researcher has been removed as head of research at Xinhua Hospital. Qiu did not respond to questions about the investigation report.

Shi says the trial in the girl should not have gone ahead if the therapy showed evidence of harm in animals.

Recent findings suggest that the investigators also found that Xinhua Hospital failed to conduct sufficient scientific assessment for the clinical trial. According to the statement, although the hospital’s ethics committee asked the research team to submit extra materials when safety evidence was lacking, it approved the trial without receiving those materials. In addition, the consent form given to the children’s family did not mention death as a risk of taking the therapy. Two members of the hospital’s ethics committee were given penalties.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine and Xinhua Hospital did not respond to questions about the investigation report.

JJ Gabriel has posted a farewell message to Manchester United fans ahead of his impending switch to Real Madrid.

Mauricio Pochettino has not taken charge of a single training session as head coach of the club, but one of his first tasks will be to deal with the fallout of a damaging exit.

Teenager Gabriel revealed in September that he wished to move away from Old Trafford, and while he was registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving to a club in the European Union once he turned 16.

A number of sides were reported to be interested in signing him, but Real Madrid have seemingly won the race for his signature.

Gabriel has confirmed his exit from United in a farewell video message posted to his Instagram page on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that ??? JJ Gabriel: “Goodbye and thank you, Man United”. https://t.co/5uXeBLHIcX.

Though there have been many reasons to be critical of United's approach to their young stars, it would be harsh to reprimand them over losing Gabriel.

It was reported earlier this year that the teenager and his entourage were disappointed about the pathway into first-team football, but the youngster only turned 16 on October 6.

Perhaps Gabriel believed he should have been fast-tracked into the XI like Lamine Yamal was at Barcelona and Spain, but the Baca winger's progression into senior football was anomalous.

It should also be noted that he will have to battle against the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in Real Madrid's team, so it remains to be seen if he is given the minutes he desires.

Though United have not necessarily conducted themselves poorly in regard to Gabriel's exit, the saga may have an unfortunate impact on their image as a fruitful hub for young talent.

United are right now engulfed in a relegation battle in the Premier League, and the atmosphere at Old Trafford has arguably never been more toxic.

The failures of the team on the pitch and the chaos behind the scenes may deter younger talents from joining United in the future, though the club's hierarchy will hope that Pochettino can restore the club's place as a premier destination.

Recent findings suggest that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Recent findings suggest that arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

Sources indicate that “That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

Industry observers note that “Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

It has been revealed that “We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

Sources indicate that “But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

Industry observers note that “Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

In a recent development, “They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to one report, Liverpool have the opportunity to snap up a full-back from a fellow European giant for a modest amount.

The Reds have found a solution to the problematic right-back position with the loan acquisition of Ronald Araujo, who was originally signed to add centre-back cover but has excelled on the flank at Anfield.

Despite the Barcelona loanee’s fine form, Jamie Carragher has implored his former club to move for a full-back in January if the right opportunity arises, and there might just be another one from Camp Nou.

As reported by Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, the LaLiga champions are prepared to sanction an exit for Alejandro Balde amid interest from Liverpool, with Barca head coach Hansi Flick indicating that the 23-year-old isn’t part of his looks.

His representative Jorge Mendes has reportedly held talks with the Merseyside club to inform them of the conditions surrounding a potential deal for the player, who’s viewed by Anfield chiefs as an ‘attractive option’.

The agent is understood to have communicated a valuation of €40m (£33m) to prospective suitors, and that figure would apply whether the deal is structured as a permanent transfer or a loan arrangement with a purchase option.

It has been revealed that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even though Balde has been overtaken by Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo in the left-back pecking order at Barcelona, Liverpool might still feel that the price point apparently quoted by Mendes would represent something of a bargain for the 23-year-old.

Catalan columnist Javier Miguel has previously hailed some ‘spectacular’ performances from the Spain international (AS), and an analysis from The Athletic highlighted his aptitude for taking on opposition full-backs whilst marauding along the left flank.

He’s also renowned for his pace, with his former agent Junior Minguella describing him as a ‘bullet’, and Flick previously spoke of how the Spain international strives to ‘get better every day’ (The Athletic).

If Kostas Tsimikas were to depart at the end of his contract next summer – certainly not an implausible scenario – then Liverpool would need to add left-back competition for Milos Kerkez, and Barcelona’s apparent readiness to offload Balde could play into our hands.

Considering the success we’ve had so far with Araujo, FSG might just be inclined to sound out the Catalan giants about potentially adding another full-back option from Flick’s squad in 2027. This could be an intriguing one to watch over the coming months.

He remained at Man City for the season ahead but has continued to struggle for minutes despite Enzo Maresca's arrival.

The 21-year-old has only started one Premier League game in this campaign so far and doubts over his future have started to rise ahead of January.

New comments around his aims for the near future and favoured position on the pitch both surely point to an inevitable departure from the Etihad in the coming months.

Lewis is bound to attract attention from more Premier League clubs and has all the tools to be a regular at the top level away from a highly competitive City squad.

Lewis is under contract at City until 2030, but seems as close as ever to exiting his boyhood club following a tough start to the campaign.

He has only appeared in six competitive games under Maresca so far, with just two appearances and 102 minutes played in the league.

Lewis detailed his aims for the future and where he would prefer to play in a recent interview with GIVEMESPORT, saying: "I’ve enjoyed playing wherever, but now I’m kind of getting that feeling where I enjoy helping the team going forward. So I think the best place to do that is in the midfield for me. Finding that joy of scoring, assisting, that’s what’s kind of driving me to that feeling.

"The goal in 12 months’ time is playing as many games as I can. Preparing myself mentally, not playing, not playing, not playing, then getting the chance to play, there’s no point in wasting that 90 minutes wishing I was playing those other games I’m playing right now. For me, [my aims] would be literally playing as many games as I can do...having that experience of playing sustained minutes and consistently.".

Lewis has only ever featured somewhat regularly at right-back for City, and their outstanding midfield depth surely means he has no chance of breaking through there anytime soon.

Sources have already exclusively revealed to Football Insider that Lewis could look to leave City in January if he continues to struggle for minutes.

His latest comments highlight a player who knows what is best for his career at 21-years-old, but will surely have to move elsewhere to fulfil his aims for the next year.

Using Carabao Cup stats, which are the biggest sample size for Lewis so far in 2026-27, it is clear to see that he stands little chance of nailing down a spot as City's main right-back anytime soon.

He ranks poorly among full-backs in the competition for chances created per 90 (0.54), duels won per 90 (4.88), aerial duels won per 90 (0.54) and defensive contributions per 90 (4.34).

With so many bodies ahead of him in midfield, such lacklustre stats only further the point that he is surely set to leave the club very soon.

Barcelona sporting director Deco has left the door wide open for Liverpool to sign Ronald Araujo permanently.

The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan in August and has made an immediate impression on the Anfield faithful, putting in a series of tremendous performances at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Reports from Spain in recent days have indicated that Merseyside chiefs are keen to take up the option to sign the defender outright for £47m, with the player also understood to be ready to stay in L4 beyond next summer.

Liverpool’s chances of securing him on a permanent basis would appear to have been greatly boosted by comments from Deco.

The Barcelona chief told Catalunya Radio’s Tot Costa: “A bit of money wouldn’t hurt us either. We’d be happy because things have gone well, and we’d be happy for him too.

Sources indicate that “Personally, I’m happy for Ronald. He’s one of the team’s leaders. He’s been through some difficult times and some happy ones at the club, and we have a good relationship.

“He’s made his decision, and we respect it. The most important thing for us is to see him happy. If he decides to stay and things carry on like this, we’d be happy with that too.”.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It seems that, if Liverpool were to sign Araujo permanently, everyone would be a winner.

The Reds would secure a player who’s been excellent for them (and get a deal done at a relatively modest fee), the defender would get to remain on Merseyside (where his family are reportedly very happy), and Barcelona would bank nearly £50m for someone they’re seemingly happy to let go.

Even with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni finally back in first-team training, both of them will realistically need a few more weeks to be properly matchday ready, so Iraola will continue to depend heavily on the Uruguayan to maintain form and fitness.

Liverpool won’t be able to activate the purchase option on Araujo until the end of the season, and it’s not implausible that he could succumb to a serious injury or see his performance levels drop in the meantime.

Right now, though, there’s no excuse for Anfield chiefs not to go all-out to secure a permanent transfer, especially with Deco indicating that Barcelona would be prepared to sanction his sale. Don’t fumble this one please, Julian Ward!

By Joel Lefevre | 18 Nov 2026 02:01.

The bottom two teams in Ligue 1 will kick off matchday 11 of the campaign Friday as Troyes welcome Le Havre to Stade de l’Aube.

Heading into this match, Troyes are 17th in the table after suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, putting them six points above the Normandy club, who lost their last league fixture 2-0 at home to Lorient.

Some improved results of late have brought Troyes back within reach of Ligue 1 safety after 10 matchdays in the top flight.

After losing five successive matches in this competition, Stephane Dumont has seen his side earn points in two of their last three contests.

One of the biggest improvements has been their poise at the back, as they have collected two clean sheets in their last three league fixtures after conceding multiple goals in five straight games.

While their defensive game is much improved, they are still struggling to create many scoring opportunities, sitting dead last in the league for major chances so far.

On Friday, they can claim consecutive Ligue 1 triumphs at Stade de l’Aube for the first time since March-April 2022, after beating Le Mans on Halloween (2-0).

ESTAC have won three of their last four home meetings with Le Havre, all in Ligue 2, and have lost just one of their last five games against them.

It is an urgent time for Le Havre, who enter this matchday six points back of Ligue 1 safety and are the only side yet to win this season.

The club have stated that this is an emergency situation and, as such, appointed Valerien Ismael as the new manager in hopes of getting out of the relegation zone.

The well-travelled coach, who was born in Strasbourg, has a reputation for turning clubs around swiftly, taking Barnsley from a team near the bottom of the Championship to a playoff position by the end of the 2020-21 campaign.

Ismael has a massive job ahead of him, to transform a side in Le Havre, who have given up the joint-second-most goals in Ligue 1 thus far (22).

He takes over a team that have suffered six consecutive defeats in this competition, while earning just one point away from home this season.

While they have not fared well against Troyes of late, Le Ciel et Marine are unbeaten against them in Ligue 1 this century, winning that last meeting in Normandy in 2003 (1-0).

Due to an ankle injury, Troyes are expected to be without Anis Ouzenadji on Friday, and Yacouba Kone is dealing with a sore knee.

From matchday nine to 10, we saw two new faces in their starting 11, with Ismael Boura and Kandet Diawara replacing Paolo Gozzi and Timothe Nkada, while Hillel Konate got the start between the sticks yet again.

As for Le Havre, Rassoul Ndiaye and Elias Jelert are doubtful because of leg injuries, while Timothee Pembele is dealing with adductor pain and unlikely to feature.

Lionel Mpasi and Felix Mambimbi are out with Achilles tendon ruptures, while Stephan Zagadou is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Troyes possible starting lineup:.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Mille, Karim, Diop; Le Douaron, Ripart, Nkada.

Le Havre possible starting lineup:.

Bodart; Sasso, Koffi, Touba; Ouziad, Ebonog, Mwanga, Richardson; Fofana, Samatta; Maja.

Ismael has a reputation for elevating his teams quickly, and against a Troyes side that are not terribly potent in front of goal, we believe the Normandy club will catch a break and pull out a narrow victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino is planning to visit former clubs and the USA national team as he looks to improve his Manchester United squad.

Shortly after the 54-year-old's appointment, he is already putting transfer looks in place as he aims to overhaul his squad, having assessed their key areas of weakness.

Speculation has immediately linked the boss with a number of his former stars, and those reports may not be wide of the mark, and he hopes to land some trusted allies.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that there is a "real chance" that Pochettino will look to land players he has worked with in the past.

That will ease their transition into his system, while he will know the exact profile of players he needs for his prepares, and could limit any errors made by the recruitment team.

A number of players in Xabi Alonso's Chelsea squad played under Pochettino, while the USMNT seems an obvious destination, as Pochettino looks to stamp his mark.

Brown told Football Insider on 17 November that Man United must back Pochettino in the transfer market if they want him to be successful, as the squad is not good enough.

Talks have been held with the board about potential backing, and while they had no initial plans to splash the cash mid-season, they may be forced to back the manager.

Revisiting former players can be a profitable avenue for newly introduced managers, and Pochettino is no different, as he begins putting plans in place for a busy mid-season window.

"Manchester United need to sign players in January, that's not a controversial thing to say," Brown told Football Insider.

Industry observers note that "Pochettino will know that, so the question is about which players? Where does he go to sign players who are going to make his side better?

"The obvious answer is, he could look at his former clubs, former players, people he trusts and people he knows can play specific roles that his system demands of them.

"Rather than trying to shoehorn his current players, or somebody the club want to bring in, into his intends, he could instead look at players he already knows well.

"There's a real chance that could be the direction he looks in, so any of those USA players, maybe even Chelsea players, could be on his list.

"Ron Atkinson always used to say, everybody can make a mistake in the transfer market, but not when it's a player you've had before.

"Pochettino will know their strengths, weaknesses, characters, everything about them, so he will know whether or not they are good fit for this squad and for Man United.

"If he then decides he wants those players and think they will improve the team, then of course, there's no reason why he wouldn't go for that.".

Since Pochettino's appointment as the new Man United manager, there have already been links with a number of former players, both with their clubs and countries.

A number of USA internationals have been linked, with some even speaking out about the speculation, but he could first be tempted to revisit a Chelsea star.

Football Insider revealed on 14 November that Malo Gusto could be among Pochettino's first signings at Old Trafford amid doubts about his future at Chelsea.

Having started just three Premier League games so far this season, reports have claimed the Frenchman is looking for a move away from Stamford Bridge.

Man United have been long-term admirers, and failed with a move in the summer transfer window, with Pochettino's apponitment potentially set to move the needle.

The Monaco midfielder is also more accomplished with the ball, and he should still be seen as the premium option, either in January or the summer.

Trey Nyoni will almost certainly become a starter in the next few years, and signing another midfielder would pose a problem in terms of guaranteeing playing time.

Szoboszlai and Gravenberch are contracted to Anfield until 2031 and 2032 respectively, so moving on either player would be difficult.

Alexis Mac Allister has been the Reds' best midfielder this season and has arguably been among the best performers in that role across the division, so losing him in the coming summer would weaken the squad.

Liverpool may soon be faced with a painful decision, with at least one of their established stars likely to head for the exit doors in the coming months.

Ornstein's enhancement represents a significant complication for Arsenal, who could now need to explore alternative attacking targets if they want to strengthen in January.

Kroupi's contract situation means Bournemouth have little reason to entertain offers, while the player's reported preference for moving abroad further weakens the Gunners' position.

Nusa would not necessarily provide the same centre-forward option as Kroupi, but his ability to operate out wide could address another area where Arsenal need greater depth.

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

The 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a new club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI data centres have massive electricity demands, which are estimated to quadruple over the next decade.Credit: Mario Tama/Getty.

Ten countries, including Germany and Brazil, at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, have pledged to do more to limit the greenhouse-gas emissions produced by the rapid development of artificial intelligence — and to use the technology to cut emissions elsewhere.

It has been revealed that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

In a recent development, how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

“The pledge brings together two priorities that must advance together: reducing the environmental footprint of AI and expanding its contribution to climate action,” remarked Mehmet Fatih Kacır, Turkey’s minister of industry and technology, on 16 November at a launch event for the initiative, called the Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge.

Some climate advocates welcomed the pledge as a necessary, if vague, step to address the growing emissions and environmental impacts caused by running AI data centres. And researchers say there are ways that the technology could be used to cut emissions, for instance by helping to integrate renewables onto power grids or by improving logistics.

Sources indicate that but it remains unknown whether such emission reductions could offset AI’s consequences for the climate. “The trillion-dollar question is whether or not those savings will outweigh those impacts we’re seeing now,” says Eric Masanet, a mechanical engineer who studies decarbonization at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Industry observers note that the rapid building of AI data centres — which are used to train and operate AI systems — has drawn increasing ire from environmental quarters because of its insatiable demand for electricity. A report this month from BloombergNEF, which provides research on the transition to clean energy, estimated that electricity demand from data centres will almost quadruple over the next decade, making up 7% of global electricity demand in 2035, and accounting for at least 2% of the world’s emissions.

In a recent development, most of that would come from the United States, where the building of data centres has been biggest and fastest, followed by China. In the race to train the most capable models, many big US technology firms are seeking to build gas-fired power plants to satisfy data centres’ energy demands, rather than waiting for permission to connect to the public power grid.

Can AI models reliably forecast extreme weather events?

Can AI models reliably forecast extreme weather events?

That’s the sort of approach the pledge aims to prevent. It calls on countries to take action to power AI infrastructure with “zero- and low-emission energy” and to improve the efficiency with which data centres use power and water for cooling. Nations that join will assess progress yearly.

The other G20 countries that signed on are South Korea and Turkey. The host country sponsored the launch of the pledge and said that it would aim to power its data centres with 60% low-carbon sources. They were joined by Andorra, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia and Uganda. More than 80 organizations endorsed the pledge, including a few large tech companies such as Nokia and Telefónica, according to a tracker from the United Nations’ International Telecommunications Union, one of the effort’s organizing bodies. However, none of the frontier AI firms has joined the pledge.

It has been revealed that given the absence of AI’s biggest emitters, some climate advocates dismissed the initiative. “The AI pledge risks giving Major Tech a green stamp without requiring it to address the real climate impacts of its infrastructure,” claims Jill McArdle, a campaigner at Beyond Fossil Fuels, an advocacy group in Berlin.

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical glitch that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

Whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

Liverpool training: Four Reds players provide Iraola with timely boost ahead of Man United clash

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.
  • With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.
  • There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor issue, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images).

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor issues.

Barring any new setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

Iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. Long may it stay that way!

Liverpool transfer news: Reds join Barcelona race for Brazilian defender amid Van Dijk doubt

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04.
  • Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved.
  • While the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04.

Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved. The Dutch defender’s contract runs until the end of the season and he has yet to reach an agreement over an extension, while Liverpool are monitoring the market.

While the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes. With his contract running until the end of the season, Van Dijk has no renewal agreement in progress and can sign a pre-contract agreement from January.

With the situation of the Dutch defender unresolved, Liverpool have entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem.

It has been revealed that according to Sports Illustrated, Liverpool have sent scouts to follow the rise of Arthur Dias closely and are now assessing the possibility of buying him from Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is one of the breakout stars of Brazilian football in 2026 and is being watched by several European clubs.

Barcelona’s interest in Arthur Dias is long-standing, as being left-footed and comfortable playing out from the back are qualities missing from manager Hansi Flick’s squad. Van Dijk, who is right-footed but also plays on the left side of central defence, would leave a gap for Liverpool to fill should he depart.

The Brazilian centre-back has a contract until December 2028 and has already seen a Tottenham Hotspur offer of £18m (€21m) rejected by Athletico Paranaense. The club’s board believes Arthur Dias should only be released for an offer of at least £25.5m (€30m) because of his high potential.

So far, Liverpool have made no formal approach to Athletico Paranaense for the young defender, but the competition is not limited to Barcelona.

Clubs such as Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also monitoring Arthur Dias, who gained international visibility with his first two call-ups to the Brazil national team in the post-World Cup international breaks.

It has been revealed that brazilian aside, Liverpool’s number four has no guaranteed future at Anfield. Despite his idol status and undisputed place in the starting line-up under manager Andoni Iraola, Van Dijk has no advanced talks with the club’s directors over his stay, with moves towards an extension expected to gather pace at the turn of the year.

The captain himself admitted in a recent interview that he plans to stay at Liverpool, but has no news on his situation.

The Spanish manager is in favour of Van Dijk staying, as the Dutchman is not only a leadership figure in the dressing room but also a pillar of the defensive system, having won 75% of his duels in this season’s Premier League.

In that context, AC Milan have emerged as one of the clubs interested in the 35-year-old defender. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is an admirer of the Dutchman and believes he can make a difference to Ruben Amorim’s project through his experience and technical quality.

Newcastle United fans think on-loan striker Nick Woltemade can solve their challenges as the club lines up a latest attacking signing in January.

Matthias Jaissle has struggled to make his mark since being appointed as Newcastle manager in August.

He oversaw a busy end to the summer window that saw the club allow German striker Woltemade to join Juventus on loan.

The 24-year-old had an immediate impact on Tyneside last season but struggled for form in the second half of the campaign.

He has impressed with the Italian giants, registering four goals and two assists in 13 appearances so far.

Newcastle's own slow start to the campaign is set to see them enter the market for a latest forward, despite Woltemade still being on their books.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo effectively replaced Woltemade in the Newcastle squad in a £52million move from Lille, but he is yet to find the net in his first seven appearances for his new club.

Will Osula has been plagued by injury complications and has one strike to his name so far this term, while fellow striker Yoane Wissa has the same record in 13 appearances up to now.

According to a upcoming report from Sky Sports' Keith Downie, Jaissle is eyeing new striker and number 10 signings in the next window, although the club are aware that landing a player in both positions is unlikely.

With Woltemade doing well away from St James' Park, Newcastle fans are adamant that he can succeed under Jaissle.

According to recent reports, one took to X to reply to the report, saying: "Recall Woltemade = striker problem sorted, then concentrate on a number 10. This saves time and a lot of money.".

He'll be after a 6'7 German. No chance you'll find one in january.

In a recent development, and one Magpies supporter wrote: "Recall Woltemade and put all the money towards a winger and a 10. He will be a much better player with better players around him!".

Theres a german playing for juve,hes scoring atm.

They will just recall Woltemade and Neave.

Jaissle is a man under pressure and so will likely not want to be seen going back to Woltemade after he contributed to the decision to let him leave at the end of the summer window.

The Newcastle boss spent the international break in their home country and gave an interview to German press about how they have kept in contact and aims for the future.

According to recent reports, he remarked: "We are continuing to follow his development very closely. I'm confident that he still has a huge career ahead of him. He is an incredibly great person and a unique footballer. We were extremely open and transparent with each other right from the start.

"At the start of the season, there was a period when he wasn't in the starting line-up and other players were ahead of him because of the way we played. He then decided to get more playing time elsewhere. That's how the move to Juve finally came about.".

Ryan Gravenberch 'not happy' with his Liverpool career teetering - expert

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ryan Gravenberch will have to improve if he is to reclaim his position at Liverpool this season.
  • That is according to experienced former Everton, Tottenham and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.
  • The 24-year-old once-untouchable appears to have been usurped by teenager Trey Nyoni, who has broken into Andoni Iraola's team in recent weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ryan Gravenberch will have to improve if he is to reclaim his position at Liverpool this season.

That is according to experienced former Everton, Tottenham and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 24-year-old once-untouchable appears to have been usurped by teenager Trey Nyoni, who has broken into Andoni Iraola's team in recent weeks.

The 19-year-old was selected from the start in midfield for the visit of Arsenal at the start of the month, with Gravenberch forced to sit on the bench in a seeming change of the guard.

The Netherlands international has been a key man for Liverpool over the last couple of years but has allowed mistakes to creep into his game this season.

Despite only signing a upcoming deal until 2032 in March, some are now even questioning Gravenberch's future at Anfield.

Gravenberch missed Liverpool's last two games before the international break through injury.

He will hope to return to the squad against Manchester United on Sunday with renewed energy, with his position under threat.

"He won't play every game. He'll probably get rested for a little bit and then Gravenberch will come in," King told Football Insider when asked about Nyoni's place in the team.

"For me, he's the future, this type of player. I like the boy [Jeremy Jacquet] they brought in at centre half as well. I like him.

According to recent reports, "I think those two players are players that can can certainly be taking Liverpool to the next step. Gravenberch will be part of the squad.

"Of course, he's not happy because he's not in the team, but that's football. There are 11 starting positions. When you've got somebody who's in there performing like this kid's performing, you're just going to have to wait your time because you'll probably get a chance.

"Maybe he picks up an injury or it might be time to rest him. But I think Gravenberch has certainly got to up his game if he's going to get a regular place back in the side because this kid is a breath of fresh air.".

Just a few months ago, Gravenberch was recognised among the best midfielders in the Premier League and the future of Liverpool's midfield.

But it has taken just a poor start to the season and some bad decisions for the midfielder to lose some of his manager's trust.

The Netherlands international was sent off for a silly challenge against Manchester City last month and gave a penalty for a needless tackle in the Carabao Cup against Chelsea.

Nyoni brings calm to the Liverpool team and until Gravenberch can again, he will be Iraola's second choice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

The defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an matter, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, this morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

The Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

The management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

He has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 07:17.
  • Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to make several changes to his Manchester United squad, with the defence expected to be a major priority over the coming transfer windows.
  • Noussair Mazraoui is among those whose long-term future at Old Trafford remains uncertain, despite previously being highly regarded by the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 07:17.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to make several changes to his Manchester United squad, with the defence expected to be a major priority over the coming transfer windows.

Noussair Mazraoui is among those whose long-term future at Old Trafford remains uncertain, despite previously being highly regarded by the club.

The Argentine is keen to assess the Morocco international in person before deciding whether to make a new contract a priority.

Mazraoui is attracting interest from clubs in both Italy and Saudi Arabia, but Pochettino wants to take a closer look at the right-back over the coming weeks before reaching a verdict on his future, according to new reports.

The 29-year-old is contracted to United until the summer of 2028, with the club also holding an option to extend his deal by a further year.

Consequently, neither party is in immediate danger of running out of time to agree fresh terms, and there is no urgency to conclude negotiations.

However, Mazraoui has endured an injury-disrupted start to the campaign, making just five Premier League appearances so far.

United are understood to be planning a 'defensive overhaul' across the next few transfer windows, although the former Bayern Munich defender could avoid the significant changes expected elsewhere in the backline.

His versatility is a major asset, having featured at right-back, left-back and centre-back, while he remains viewed as a potentially important part of the project at Old Trafford.

Nevertheless, Mazraoui will need to impress Pochettino before the manager decides whether to commit to him for the longer term.

United's defensive problems have plagued the club for several seasons, and simply making one or two adjustments is unlikely to provide the necessary solution.

Pochettino, therefore, needs to take a wider view of the backline, with multiple additions potentially required across the defensive positions.

Left-back should be a particularly vital area of focus, while further reinforcements at centre-back and right-back could also be needed depending on who survives the anticipated overhaul.

Mazraoui's ability to cover several positions could make him a useful squad member, but his injury record and contract situation mean that his future cannot be taken for granted.

Ultimately, Pochettino must establish which defenders can form part of his long-term plans before United commit significant resources to rebuilding their defence.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

In a recent development, the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

According to recent reports, it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager noted. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

According to recent reports, united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Recent findings suggest that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and rapidly.

In a recent development, speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick remarked: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

Industry observers note that “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

It has been revealed that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Sources indicate that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

Sources indicate that when asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

Sources indicate that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

Michael Carrick has made two changes to the side which drew against Fulham. Amad Diallo returns to the fold after a spell on the sidelines with an injury, replacing Marcus Rashford, who drops to the bench. The other alteration comes in defence, with Diogo Dalot departing for Leny Yoro.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

It has been revealed that man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

According to recent reports, the strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

It has been revealed that the spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after major-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Latest Update: Ronaldinho makes return at age of 46: Brazil legend plays full first-half for Italian third-tier team and hints he may play again despite 'publicity stunt' criticism

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.
  • The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar revealed his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar revealed his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida said in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his new side.

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

Sources indicate that he started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

Recent findings suggest that 'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'.

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

  • Liverpool have taken a significant step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister's long-term future by opening contract negotiations with the midfielder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:40.

Liverpool have taken a significant step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister's long-term future by opening contract negotiations with the midfielder.

The Argentina international has been keen to extend his stay at Anfield, but there had been growing frustration over the lack of progress.

However, fresh claims suggest the Reds have finally changed their stance and begun discussions over a upcoming deal.

According to reliable Argentine journalist Cesar Luis Merlo (via Sport Witness), Liverpool have opened negotiations with Mac Allister over a contract extension.

The 27-year-old's current agreement runs until June 2028, meaning the Reds have made an early move to keep him at Anfield beyond that date.

There is no agreement in place yet, and Merlo has not disclosed any proposed salary or contract length, although the coming weeks could provide a clearer indication of whether both parties can reach a compromise.

The development represents a change from the situation described by Mac Allister's father and agent, Carlos, who told ESPN Brazil just days ago that Liverpool had not started negotiations.

The long-serving star has also previously voiced his disappointment at the lack of an offer, admitting in September that he was "very, very sad" about the situation, particularly after teammates Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai had been offered newly introduced contracts.

More recently, Mac Allister attempted to reassure supporters, expressing hope that the club's board would reconsider its position.

Liverpool's reported change of heart could reflect Mac Allister's importance to Andoni Iraola's plans, with the £55m enforcer continuing to receive regular opportunities.

Starting eight of the Reds' ten Premier League matches and three of their four Champions League fixtures, he remains a prominent part of the team's midfield setup.

That level of involvement makes it difficult to justify allowing uncertainty over his future to continue, particularly when he has consistently indicated a desire to remain at Anfield.

There is still work to do before an agreement is reached, but opening discussions is an encouraging development for Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister has made his feelings clear, and the club now appears to be responding. Keeping an established midfielder of his importance could prove a sensible decision as Iraola continues shaping his squad.

AC Milan talent Akram Jadid is making a name for himself on the international stage, with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s.

At the Stadio Olimpico in Sousse, the Milan U18s striker scored a hat-trick in the 5-1 win over Tunisia. Not only that, but he got his three goals in just five minutes. It was a performance that quickly gained traction on social media, where videos of his goals are circulating widely.

Sources indicate that the match opened with Morocco taking the lead through Hatim Dabdoubi in the 24th minute. After half-time, Mohamed Aziz Abdelbaki levelled things on the hour mark, before Aymane Aït Hammou restored the lead with six minutes to go.

Then Jadid entered the scene. He netted 89th minute with his left foot, converted a penalty to make it 4-1 in the 92nd minute and completed his hat-trick in the 94th minute, scoring with his right foot.

He is one to look out for in the future, with promotion to the Primavera and eventually the Futuro seeming like a certainty at this point. He has trained with the first team, and went viral for having scored over 700 goals in the youth teams to this point.

#37677. The psychology of imaginary friends — and why they are good for kids

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (994 w)
