The psychology of imaginary friends — and why they are good for kids

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Projecting thoughts and feelings onto imagined friends helps children to develop their social skills.Credit: Oscar Wong/Getty.
  • The Imagination Scientist: Researching Pretend Beings and their Creators Paige E.
  • Industry observers note that when my brother Arnie was about four years old, he began chatting about an imaginary and invisible companion named Embley, who seemingly travelled with him everywhere.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Projecting thoughts and feelings onto imagined friends helps children to develop their social skills.Credit: Oscar Wong/Getty.

The Imagination Scientist: Researching Pretend Beings and their Creators Paige E. Davis Oxford Univ. Press (2026).

Industry observers note that when my brother Arnie was about four years old, he began chatting about an imaginary and invisible companion named Embley, who seemingly travelled with him everywhere. During a 1970s epidemic of whooping cough (linked to an unwarranted vaccine-safety scare), Arnie became sick with this braying cough, which kept him home from school for more than six weeks.

In a recent development, embley was the “same size, age and disposition as me”, my brother recalled later, and he offered companionship and “exploration of potential sources of adventure”. Although he could not remember other aspects of Embley’s personality or appearance, my brother did add one pertinent detail: “He was always available.”.

The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?

The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?

I thought of Embley while reading The Imagination Scientist, a deeply researched and highly entertaining look at the world of imaginary companions by developmental psychologist Paige Davis.

Recent findings suggest that it seems that Embley exemplified several features of children’s imaginary friends: he was comforting and constant; he played with my brother; and he perhaps enabled him to process fear and cope with the stress of a serious illness. He might also have insulated my brother from loneliness while his older siblings were at school. Most importantly, my brother himself created Embley’s mind.

That last characteristic of an imaginary friend is key, asserts Davis. “My theory is that the most important aspect of the imaginary creature, no matter whether it is seen or unseen, lies in the creation of its mind by the child,” she writes. “To have an invisible friend or personified object considered as an imaginary companion, the child must create, conceptualize, and interact with the separate and distinct mind.”.

According to recent reports, davis opens a wardrobe door, Narnia-style, into a whimsical world inhabited by imaginary companions — some invisible, others personified in a doll or stuffed toy. Up to 65% of children up to the age of seven have had imaginary companions at some stage, according to research by psychologist Marjorie Taylor. Some imaginary friends disappear at the end of childhood, others continue to accompany their creators into adolescence. But not all made-up playmates are friendly: some are a nuisance and might even pick fights with their creators (or vice versa).

Generally, there’s nothing pathological about creating a pretend friend, Davis contends. On the contrary, the presence of such a pal might fortify the child as they deal with transitions or scary situations. Children do understand the distinction between fantasy friends and real ones, and can grasp this difference as young as three years old. “Imaginary friends are a very common, developmentally appropriate phenomena that occurs in multiple cultures around the world,” Davis writes. They “are not only a healthy form of play, but they can be extremely enjoyable for their creator”.

Imaginary friends can offer a child a sense of protection.Credit: Ian Nolan/Getty.

They’re also great fun to read about. I laughed aloud as I learnt about some of the “human, non-human, and superhuman” forms that Davis has encountered while interviewing children for her research. “I’ve had blue blobs, yellow birds, and rainbow hair,” she writes, “a fire-boy who erupts like a volcano when he becomes angry” and “a genderless imaginary companion that snacks on lightbulbs”. One little girl had twin imaginary companions, who themselves had made their own imaginary friend, “which I thought was quite meta”, she writes.

Recent findings suggest that davis first began immersing herself in the world of imaginary companions as a PhD student at the University of Durham, UK. I “thought about how much fun it would be to work with children, play, and imagination for a job”, Davis writes. It’s clear that, a decade and a half later, she still derives a delicious glee from listening to the odd observations of children (including her two sons).

According to recent reports, in one of her early studies, Davis and her colleagues looked at the relationship between imaginary companions and “theory of mind”, an umbrella term that involves understanding that other people have emotions, thoughts and ideas, just as we do. Thus, writes Davis, “children with a theory of mind are able to put themselves in another person’s shoes to infer what they may be thinking or feeling.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:40.
  • Barcelona’s winter transfer window is becoming seriously complicated, with sporting director Deco reportedly forced to abandon a second defensive target after Jonathan Tah.
  • La Liga leaders Barcelona have seen their lead over Real Madrid shrink in recent weeks, with Jose Mourinho’s side now only three points behind after 12 games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:40.

Barcelona’s winter transfer window is becoming seriously complicated, with sporting director Deco reportedly forced to abandon a second defensive target after Jonathan Tah. Hansi Flick has clearly expressed his desire for defensive reinforcements, but the priority deals appear difficult to complete.

La Liga leaders Barcelona have seen their lead over Real Madrid shrink in recent weeks, with Jose Mourinho’s side now only three points behind after 12 games.

In a recent development, the title race is expected to be fiercely contested this season and the Catalans will need reinforcements to achieve their objectives. The stated winter priority is to sign a centre-back, but finding the perfect profile, at the right price, is no easy task.

It has been revealed that deco and Barcelona’s hierarchy have positioned themselves for Alessandro Bastoni, among others, but the chances of completing his arrival are slim. In recent days, the Tah option has also closed, as Bayern Munich have no intention of letting him leave. Now another deal can be forgotten about at Barcelona, the one leading to Josko Gvardiol.

According to information gathered by AS, the Manchester City defender matched the profile Barcelona are looking for, namely a centre-back capable of playing at left-back.

The problem is that the Croatia international has extended his contract with Manchester City until 2031 and a transfer ‘seems impossible’, the Spanish outlet reports.

It has been revealed that possible financial or sporting sanctions threatening Manchester City could have eventually unblocked the situation, but nothing will be confirmed before 2027. The Catalans therefore find themselves somewhat in an impasse, and signing the two or three priority defensive targets is becoming seriously complicated.

Barcelona’s hierarchy will probably have to aim a little lower, particularly as the budget is far from unlimited in Catalonia. The sale of Alejandro Balde, reportedly set to leave, could however swell the winter transfer budget.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30.
  • Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.
  • Despite Xabi Alonso acknowledging that the midfielder was carrying a fitness issue into the game at Sunderland before the November international break, Caicedo played the full 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30.

Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

Despite Xabi Alonso acknowledging that the midfielder was carrying a fitness issue into the game at Sunderland before the November international break, Caicedo played the full 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light.

Prior to representing his country across two matches, the Blues star himself admitted that he was not fully fit, yet intended to feature in both games.

As well as playing 84 minutes against Costa Rica at the weekend, Caicedo featured for 45 minutes versus Bolivia on Tuesday night.

However, it has since been revealed that the 25-year-old requested to be withdrawn at half time.

Speaking to reporter Johanna Calderon after the Bolivia match, Caicedo suggested that he did not want to risk his fitness in the second half.

In an video posted on X, he said: "I wasn’t feeling too well, so I asked to come off.

"I have another commitment with my club, so I’m trying to get there as soon as possible and recover.".

Not only does Caicedo now face a long-haul flight from Ecuador, he is giving up five hours of recovery due to the time difference between Guayaquil and London.

When you factor in tiredness to add to the injury issue that he is at the moment trying to protect, Caicedo should not be starting the game with Leeds.

Jordan Henderson was not called up by England, whereas Romeo Lavia played on Sunday night having missed Belgium's first of two UEFA Nations game during the international break.

Starting that pair and having Caicedo on the substitutes' bench is the only scenario that makes sense for Alonso.

Striker Che Adams claims Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is big on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be substantial on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

Industry observers note that ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He remarked to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ stated Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

Sources indicate that ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

Chelsea injury news: Xabi Alonso in double boost ahead of Leeds United showdown

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:58.
  • Chelsea have been handed a double injury boost ahead after Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino both represented Argentina on Tuesday night.
  • Martinez and Anselmino were called up by Lionel Scaloni despite spending weeks and months on the sidelines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:58.

Chelsea have been handed a double injury boost ahead after Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino both represented Argentina on Tuesday night.

Martinez and Anselmino were called up by Lionel Scaloni despite spending weeks and months on the sidelines.

While goalkeeper Martinez had been unavailable with a fractured jaw since October 17, Anselmino has not played any competitive minutes for Chelsea in 2026-27 due to a hamstring injury.

However, the pair featured as Argentina cruised to a 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in Cordoba.

Starting between the sticks wearing a protective mask, Martinez played the full 90 minutes, albeit only having to make two saves during a one-sided contest.

Meanwhile, Anselmino was introduced as a 71st-minute substitute as the former world champions saw out the win.

Anselmino's outing - his first for Argentina - is particularly notable because it is his first since a 29-minute appearance in a pre-season friendly versus Johor DT on August 9.

When Moises Caicedo has provided a further fitness concern for Xabi Alonso, having Martinez and Anselmino come through unscathed for Argentina is a welcome boost.

Alonso must now decide whether to retain Mike Penders for Saturday's Premier League game with Leeds United or hand an immediate recall to Martinez.

Given the time difference and Penders having largely impressed in his absence, Martinez may expect to be named on the substitutes' bench.

Although it is possible that Anselmino will not feature in Chelsea's squad versus Leeds, Alonso requires an extra central-defensive option due to Maxence Lacroix being expected to be sidelined until January.

Realistically, the 21-year-old could be handed a start for the Blues' Under-21s ranks before coming into contention for the first team.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 10:15.
  • Lacking game time at Barcelona, Alejandro Balde is looking for a way out in January, with Paris Saint-Germain only just appearing in the picture.
  • Industry observers note that alejandro Balde is set to be one of the talking points of the winter transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 10:15.

Lacking game time at Barcelona, Alejandro Balde is looking for a way out in January, with Paris Saint-Germain only just appearing in the picture.

Industry observers note that alejandro Balde is set to be one of the talking points of the winter transfer window. Struggling at Barcelona, where his game time has fallen considerably, the 23-year-old left-back is considering leaving to find a bigger role elsewhere.

His record this season is particularly meagre, with five appearances and only 124 minutes played. It is a situation that contrasts sharply with the status the Spaniard enjoyed in Catalonia until very recently.

Recent findings suggest that according to the latest information from Spain and Italy, several clubs are following his situation. Juventus are considering a loan, while Monaco are eyeing a bigger move. Now Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United have also entered the fray.

Manchester United are reportedly going all out to sign Balde in January.

According to TEAMtalk, the club’s recruitment department believes the left-back has a high ceiling and Barcelona are open to a loan, which would allow Manchester United to assess him before committing to a permanent deal.

The same report states Balde is willing to move to the Premier League and that his relationship with Barcelona manager Hansi Flick is ‘completely broken and glacial’.

Recent findings suggest that fabrizio Romano has described the chance of a January exit as ‘serious and concrete’, adding that Balde is ‘genuinely ready to consider leaving’ and exploring options with his agent, Jorge Mendes. Manchester United were interested in the summer but did not proceed, with Balde considered too expensive for a left-back, in talks said to have involved a fee of €50m-€55m (£42.5m-£46.5m) and a net salary of more than €5m (£4.3m).

Industry observers note that valued at around €40m (£34m), the Barcelona player represents a market opportunity for Paris Saint-Germain. At 23, Balde already has significant experience at the highest level and still has room for improvement.

Quick and explosive, he fits the profile of a modern full-back and offers better guarantees than Lucas Digne, the disappointing summer signing. His ability to get in behind and create overloads would give Luis Enrique’s team another attacking dimension, and the move could also be a fresh start for a player who has lost confidence and continuity at Barcelona, not least because Luis Enrique rotates his starting line-up heavily.

The main obstacle is Nuno Mendes, who owns the left-back position at Paris Saint-Germain and is one of the best players in the world in that role, if not the best.

At 24, the Portuguese is a major part of the club’s project, and the left-footed Balde cannot play on the right side of defence, unless the manager comes up with something.

Luis Enrique also generally prefers a right-footed winger on the left, so Paris Saint-Germain could sign an excellent player without offering him a lasting prospect of starting, with a real risk of frustration.

Fabio Capello recalled what Franco Baresi meant to him as a player and captain, while commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s bold declarations too.

Few players mean more to a club – if any – than Baresi meant to Milan. The centre-back reinvented the role and became a symbol of one of the most dominant eras in the history of the sport, as well as an icon in the eyes of the fans who adored him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, capello was lucky enough to coach the No.6 and he spoke about Baresi’s greatness on Andrea Longoni’s YouTube channel ‘Milan Hello’. His words were relayed by MilanNews, and the emotion was clear in his voice.

“He was important for what he conveyed to the other players when they came to play for Milan. I’m talking about champions, important players, foreigners, of all qualities. They saw in him the man who conveyed the history of Milan,” he stated.

“Franco didn’t talk much in the dressing room, but when he did, he was listened to because you could feel his words came from the heart, you could feel they were something important for everyone.”.

Last night, Capello was interviewed by Sky and he commented on Cardinale’s words, who has been making some quite bold pledges about Milan’s future in recent weeks.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s promising a lot with his words, I read everything he states. Now I’m waiting for him, I’m waiting for the results. I want to see if he’ll do what he’s saying, if he has a plan and a real idea of ​​where he wants to get to.

“Berlusconi had also promised great things, but then he surrounded himself with people who knew about football. Besides the players, you also need to create a staff that follows you and understands your ideas.

Recent findings suggest that “Now I don’t know if this staff has already been chosen, he keeps talking about newly introduced sporting directors, about new people who will join Milan. Let’s see what he can do. The promises are great, we’ll see what the results will be.”.

Tech Report: Secrets of the vampires: genomes reveal how these bats live off blood alone

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All the better to eat you with: vampire bats (such as this common vampire bat, Desmodus rotundus) have an array of genetic adaptations that allow them to subsist on blood.Credit: Joel Sartore/Photo Ark/Nature Picture Library.
  • A foraging vampire bat slices into sleeping prey and laps up about half of its own body weight in blood, causing its belly to balloon.
  • The study1, posted on the preprint server bioRxiv on 7 November before being peer reviewed, provides a “high-resolution look into what it takes to build a vampire bat”, says Jasmin Camacho, an evolutionary developmental biologist at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research in Kansas City, Missouri, who was not involved in the research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All the better to eat you with: vampire bats (such as this common vampire bat, Desmodus rotundus) have an array of genetic adaptations that allow them to subsist on blood.Credit: Joel Sartore/Photo Ark/Nature Picture Library.

A foraging vampire bat slices into sleeping prey and laps up about half of its own body weight in blood, causing its belly to balloon. Now, an analysis of the bats’ genomes and organs offers clues to how they stomach this gory diet.

The study1, posted on the preprint server bioRxiv on 7 November before being peer reviewed, provides a “high-resolution look into what it takes to build a vampire bat”, says Jasmin Camacho, an evolutionary developmental biologist at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research in Kansas City, Missouri, who was not involved in the research. “It’s one of the first times we can really see what those molecular signatures of being a blood specialist look like.”.

Sources indicate that blood is a challenging meal: it contains mostly water, little sugar and fat, and toxic amounts of iron. Yet all three species of vampire bat survive exclusively on blood after reaching adulthood.

Industry observers note that to understand how they pull this off, Michael Hiller, an evolutionary genomicist at the Senckenberg Research Institute in Frankfurt, Germany, and his colleagues generated genomes for all three vampire-bat species (Desmodus rotundus, Diaemus youngii and Diphylla ecaudata) and three other species of bat. They then compared the genomes. They also analysed gene activity in six organs for two of the vampire species and four species of non-vampiric bats.

The stomach stood out. In most mammals, the stomach bathes food in acid to aid digestion. In vampire bats, however, the researchers found that the organ has been repurposed into a stretchy, pH-neutral storage sac lined with thick layers of connective tissue that help it to expand after a feast.

Vampire bats’ stomachs can expand enormously to accommodate their meals of blood. Credit: Jon Flanders.

Recent findings suggest that to shed excess water rapidly so that the bats can fly home, their stomachs ramp up activity of a fluid-transporting gene that is typically active in salivary and sweat glands by more than 900-fold, the analysis found. The function of these vampire-bat stomachs has changed so much from those of other mammals that the organs perhaps “deserve a different name”, Hiller says.

Sources indicate that despite the lack of fat in blood, the bats still retain some genes for digesting lipids. The activity of these genes is dialled down in adulthood but might enable nursing pups to digest their mother’s fat-rich milk before switching to blood after weaning, says Ken Welch Jr, a comparative physiologist at the University of Toronto in Canada. But the bats have lost some genes altogether, such as ones known to help animals to distinguish between sweet and bitter tastes2.

Using mosquitoes to vaccinate bats could curb the spread of deadly diseases.

His game by numbers vs. Wales: 89 minutes played 80 touches 56/67 successful passes 15 passes into final third 4/5 duels won 4/7 accurate long balls 3 tackles 2 chances created 2 clearances 2x possessions won 1/1 shots on target 1 goal MOTM performance. ⭐️.

As expected, the Portuguese media were full of praise for Fernandes after the Wales game.

ZeroZero called Fernandes "decisive" and praised the attacker for helping Portugal to navigate their way through the latter stages after being reduced to 10 men; he was handed a rating of 7.8/10.

A Bola focused on Fernandes' stunning goal in the early stages and also praised his passing ability, having set up chances for both Joao Cancelo and Goncalo Ramos.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough campaign for Man United, who currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table.

Fernandes has been far from his best for most of the campaign, but he has still managed to come up with six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the club this term.

There is presently speculation surrounding Fernandes' future at Old Trafford, with the Portuguese allegedly turning down the latest offer from Man United to renew his contract.

Fernandes is allegedly waiting to see what direction the club move in under Pochettino before making any firm decisions on his future with the 20-time English champions.

The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

📅 11 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (7037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered.
  • How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.
  • It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Recent findings suggest that their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

It has been revealed that this is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

Recent findings suggest that the midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

In a recent development, this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

Recent findings suggest that they are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

Sources indicate that in the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other massive signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk.

In a recent development, in fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b.

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their big summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

"It's a GEM" 💎 A beautiful strike from Jérémy Doku to double Man City's lead! https://t.co/lCUFfQmdLC.

Industry observers note that there were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW.

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

According to recent reports, “Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

Recent findings suggest that “It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

Recent findings suggest that “Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”.

Maresca noted City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”.

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

Recent findings suggest that “Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”.

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

Industry observers note that “The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”.

According to recent reports, the Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

Sources indicate that “The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

Sources indicate that “You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”.

6 - A team have started with six straight wins in just two of the last seven Premier Legue seasons (since 2020-21): Manchester City in 2023-24 and Manchester City in 2026-27. Defiance. https://t.co/fxjmoHPeoM.

It has been revealed that speaking after the game, the City midfielder told Sky Sports: “We’ve shown real togetherness and fight. It’s a tough place to come and it’s challenging.

“We really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well. We’ve shown courage and three points is good. I thought we did really well to quieten the crowd. We struggled in the first half a little bit, but in the second half we were a lot better.”.

Industry observers note that "This is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time... I'm so proud of everyone" Erling Haaland on Manchester City's win over Liverpool at Anfield. https://t.co/r3g5JgxX66.

Erling Haaland soaks up the applause of the Man City fans at full-time at Anfield. https://t.co/JozZ9VFDZ9.

City have emphatically passed the Anfield test, despite all the drama and uncertainty generated by the guilty verdict. The visitors scored three goals without reply through Haaland, Doku and Cherki, after Gravenberch was sent off. City have six wins from as many games, while Liverpool suffer their first defeat under Iraola.

Van Dijk clatters into Cherki and the Liverpool captain is deservedly booked. He can have no complaints about that.

There will be three minutes of added time to end this game.

In a recent development, the game is no longer a contest. It is now an exhibition. City fans have been brazen all afternoon and they are going to revel in this situation, as the stadium empties.

News breaks that City had been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.

Telegraph Sport understands that Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were contacted in advance of the email to the other 15 clubs.

In a letter to fans, a defiant Khaldoon Al Mubarak, City’s chairman, expresses complete confidence that his club would be vindicated.

In a recent development, “There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club,” he writes. “We will not give them that opportunity.”.

According to recent reports, with the football world still making sense of the news, Tony Pulis admits to feeling “cheated”. His Stoke City side were defeated by Manchester City in the 2011 FA Cup final, during the 2009-23 period.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali then likens City’s transgressions to “doping” before Mauricio Pochettino, whose Spurs side were often in the hunt with City for major trophies during his time as manager, says that football has “lived through a period of deception”.

The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It also discloses that image rights had been inflated and key witnesses had lied.

Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group, appears helpless when questioned about the verdict’s findings at the European Football Clubs’ general assembly in Copenhagen by Sky News.

An unblinking Soriano then features in a video statement published by City in which he claimed their guilty verdict was based on “a single false accusation”.

With City on the ropes, Pep Guardiola releases a statement in support of his former club, assuring supporters that “we will get through this together”.

The Prime Minister indicates that he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners, but after significant backlash, No 10 moves to clarify his reaction saying that “if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences”.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

There was also a nod to Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose Football Leaks documents prompted the Premier League’s investigation into City:.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission mentioned. I think that’s what’s worried me.”.

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Recent findings suggest that since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

Recent findings suggest that city have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca noted, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:31, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:32.

Arsenal will resume their Premier League campaign with a clash against Newcastle United on Saturday.

The Gunners are presently top of the Premier League table, five points clear of second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Arsenal's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their fixture against Newcastle, who sit 12th in England's top flight.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Brentford).

Saka sustained a severe quad injury during Arsenal's 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich, and the England international is not expected back until early December.

Industry News: Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (771 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a new style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

According to recent reports, asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he said: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

Industry observers note that ‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  indicates his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some newly introduced faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

In a recent development, ‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager said: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

In a recent development, ‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

In a recent development, but the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.

#37574. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1278 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31.
  • Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England.
  • It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31.

Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England.

It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record. At 16, the Englishman has already been the youngest player to score in the Premier League, to play in the Champions League and to win the English league title.

This week, he added two more marks to the list: he became the youngest player to represent the England Under-21s and, three days later, the youngest to score for the side, surpassing records that belonged to Jude Bellingham.

Recent findings suggest that the question is not only how many more records he can break, but what makes Dowman such a special talent and how far his characteristics can take him. The combination of individual skill, ball carrying, strength to compete physically and understanding of the game helps to explain why he can already produce against much older opponents.

Dowman was born on 31 December 2009 and joined Arsenal as a child. His progress through the youth ranks was so rapid that, at 13, he was already playing for the Under-18s. In September 2024, aged 14 years and eight months, he made his debut in the UEFA Youth League, an Under-19 competition, and became the youngest scorer in the history of the tournament.

The midfielder began training with the first team at 14 and took part in the 2025 pre-season. In August of that year, aged 15 years and 235 days, he made his Premier League debut against Leeds United. He was the second-youngest player to appear in the competition’s history, behind only Ethan Nwaneri, his Arsenal team-mate.

Industry observers note that in November 2025, an even more significant milestone arrived. Coming on in the 3-0 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the tournament’s history, aged 15 years and 308 days. He was also the first 15-year-old to play in the competition.

The 2025-26 season brought two more high-profile records. In March, he scored against Everton and, aged 16 years and 73 days, became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, beating James Vaughan’s mark by 197 days.

Industry observers note that months later, he went down in Arsenal history as the youngest player to win the Premier League. The medal came at 16 years and 144 days, when the club ended a 22-year wait for the title. In October, he received three Guinness World Records certificates for the achievements.

Now, the England Under-21s have added two more chapters. Dowman made his debut for the side against Portugal on 13 November, aged 16 years and 317 days, surpassing Bellingham’s mark as the youngest player to represent the age group. On the following Monday, he started for the first time and scored the winning goal against France, aged 16 years and 320 days. Bellingham had scored his first Under-21 goal aged 17 years and 67 days.

Records broken for Arsenal and England (born 31/12/2009).

If he scores for the senior England team before 12/11/2027, Dowman will surpass Wayne Rooney (17 years and 317 days, in 2003) as the youngest scorer for England.

Recent findings suggest that age in years (y) and days (d) on the date of each record. n/a = previous holder not confirmed by an official source. Data up to 17/11/2026.

Sources: Arsenal, Premier League, ESPN and TNT Sports.

It has been revealed that dowman’s main characteristic is his ability to carry the ball and beat opponents. He finds it easy to receive under pressure, shield possession with his body and change direction in tight spaces. He does not rely on straight-line speed alone: he uses feints, changes of pace and short movements to unbalance defenders.

Recent findings suggest that dowman already had a physique that allowed him to compete with older players, but he has also developed an intelligent way of using his body to protect the ball. That explains why he does not seem so intimidated when facing professional defenders.

Left-footed, he usually plays on the right, from where he can cut inside and use his dominant foot. The position also allows him to receive wide, draw the opposing full-back and choose between accelerating towards the box, combining with a team-mate or finding a pass inside. His ball control and ability to change the direction of play make him a particularly difficult threat to handle one-on-one.

It has been revealed that but reducing him to a dribbling winger would ignore an key part of his repertoire. Dowman also has experience playing as an attacking midfielder and in deeper roles. In the youth ranks, he even played as a deep-lying midfielder. This variety helped him develop a broader understanding of space and the different roles on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that versatility is an advantage for Arteta. At Arsenal, Dowman has already been used on the right and in central positions. When he receives between the lines, he can turn quickly and carry the ball towards the opposition defence. If he starts wide, he can attack the space between full-back and centre-back, moving closer to the box to shoot or take part in a combination.

There are also signs that his play without the ball matches his technical quality. In the win over France, Lee Carsley highlighted the teenager’s defensive performance, as he dropped back to intercept a pass and joined the pressing of opponents. A willingness to recover, press and take part in collective actions is an key requirement for earning a place in a side like Arteta’s.

Dowman’s rise inevitably prompts comparisons. His path recalls, in some respects, that of Nwaneri, who also made his Arsenal debut very young and had to find space in a competitive squad. Both came through the youth ranks playing in central positions, but had their first opportunities in the first team on the right.

According to recent reports, the difference is that Dowman seems to have an even clearer ability to carry the ball at speed and beat opponents one-on-one. That does not mean it is possible to determine who will have the more successful career.

Arsenal also have reason to manage expectations. The recent episode against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup highlighted one area of concern. After suffering a heavy challenge, the teenager reacted and was sent off, receiving a three-match ban. Arteta criticised the player publicly and mentioned professional football is not an environment protected from provocation and the consequences of one’s own actions.

In a recent development, there is also the question of workload. A player who starts playing professional matches so early needs physical and emotional support. Arsenal have recent experience of integrating young players such as Saka, Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly, but each athlete has his own process.

His first professional contract will be signed when he turns 17 on 31 December, after he agreed a pre-contract with Arsenal in January. The decision to stay at the club is important for the continuity of a development that has been closely monitored since the youth ranks.

The path to the senior England team is also open, but does not need to be taken immediately. Bellingham, who lost the Under-21 records to Dowman, played only four matches at that level before being promoted to the senior team.

For now, the best way to assess Dowman is to look at what he can already do, without turning every record into a career prediction. The rest depends on development, opportunities and careful management.

US Supreme Court rebuffs White House effort to cut research grants

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Supreme Court’s decision not to take up a dispute over federal research grants hands a win to scientists.Credit: Kevin Dietsch/Getty.
  • The US Supreme Court has dealt a blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to terminate research grants it deemed at odds with its political priorities.
  • The court said today that it would, for now, not intervene in a landmark legal battle over the cancellation of research grants by the US National Science Foundation (NSF) and four other federal agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Supreme Court’s decision not to take up a dispute over federal research grants hands a win to scientists.Credit: Kevin Dietsch/Getty.

The US Supreme Court has dealt a blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to terminate research grants it deemed at odds with its political priorities.

The court said today that it would, for now, not intervene in a landmark legal battle over the cancellation of research grants by the US National Science Foundation (NSF) and four other federal agencies. The court’s decision leaves in place several lower-court rulings that came out this year and last and required the reinstatement of hundreds of cancelled awards while a lawsuit brought by a group of scientists against the government proceeds.

Since early 2025, US President Donald Trump’s administration has cancelled thousands of grants from agencies such as the US National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the NSF. Many of the cancelled grants were for studies that contained terms that the administration remarked ran counter to its priorities, such as “climate change,” “equity” and “gender”. In response, a group of University of California researchers whose grants had been terminated sued the administration. Lower courts have repeatedly sided with the scientists, finding that the government had penalized academic researchers based on their viewpoints and that this likely violated the US Constitution’s First Amendment, which protects freedom of speech and other activities.

Judge rules against NIH grant cuts — and calls them discriminatory.

Judge rules against NIH grant cuts — and calls them discriminatory.

The Supreme Court’s refusal to hear the case is a relief to scientists whose work was left in limbo, and leaves protections for their reinstated funding in place. “The denial is terrific news,” says Claudia Polsky, a lawyer for the University of California researchers. The denial came only three days after the case was considered on 13 November, and none of the nine justices publicly dissented from the decision. “Those are all of the best signs one could have that the Supreme Court really did not buy the government's argument,” Polsky says.

The White House referred Nature to the US Department of Justice, which said that it would “continue to litigate” the order by one of the lower courts that “currently prevents the cancellation of certain federal research grants supporting diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives within the University of California system”.

Sources indicate that the Supreme Court’s decision not to take up the case now is not the final word on grant terminations. The lower courts found that the researchers were likely to succeed, rather than issuing a final judgment. Once a final ruling is issued, it could be appealed, potentially bringing the case back before the Supreme Court.

The case kicked off in June 2025, when Neeta Thakur, a physician who studies marginalized communities, and five other researchers at the University of California who had had federal grants terminated sued the Trump administration. The researchers argued that the cancellations were arbitrary and unlawfully penalized scientists whose work clashed with the White House’s political agenda.

The same month, judge Rita Lin at the US District Court for the Northern District of California ordered the NSF, the Environmental Protection Agency and the National Endowment for the Humanities to reinstate the University of California researchers’ grants. The plaintiffs had a “substantial likelihood that their funding was terminated based on the viewpoint expressed in their grant proposals”, Lin wrote.

Can NIH-funded research on racism and health survive Trump’s cuts?

Can NIH-funded research on racism and health survive Trump’s cuts?

In August 2025, the Supreme Court issued a ruling in a separate case about the termination of around 800 NIH grants. The court ruled that federal district courts — such as the one that originally ruled in favour of Thakur — cannot reinstate cancelled grants by invoking a law called the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), which requires federal agencies to follow proper procedures and justify their decisions. Some lower courts had used this reasoning to reinstate terminated grants.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dundee have paid tribute to one of their all-time greats following the death of Bobby Wilson at the age of 83.

A member of the club's Hall of Fame, the right-back played 411 times for the Dark Blues across 11 seasons after joining from Cowdenbeath in 1966 and lifted the League Cup in 1973.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He still holds the club record for most European appearances (17) and was a key part of the Dundee side that reached the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup semi-finals in 1968, losing to Don Revie's Leeds.

Wilson scored Dundee's only goal in the tie, an equaliser in the 1-1 first leg draw at Dens Park, before Bobby Ancell's side went down to a 1-0 defeat in the second leg at Elland Road.

Recent findings suggest that he was also part of Dundee's last major trophy success, which was achieved in 1973 with a 1-0 win over Celtic in the final of the League Cup. Wilson provided the delivery for Gordon Wallace to score the only goal.

Wilson was inducted into Dundee's Hall of Fame in 2013 on the 40th anniversary of that victory.

After leaving Dens Park, he managed Raith Rovers as well as Highland League sides Lossiemouth and Keith before a 10-year tenure at Ross County, overseeing their entry to the Scottish League in 1994.

According to recent reports, "Everyone at the club sends their condolences to Bobby's family and friends at this very difficult time," stated a Dundee statement. "Comfortably in the top 10 of most appearances for the club, Bobby retains a place in the hearts of Dundee fans as a member of the last team to bring silverware back to Dens.".

Ross County also paid tribute in a statement which read: "We are deeply saddened by the passing of our former manager, Bobby Wilson, whose leadership and dedication played a key role in transforming the club during our Highland League days and gaining entry into the Scottish Football League.

In a recent development, "His commitment and passion will never be forgotten, and his legacy will live on in the hearts of everyone connected to the club. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland will soon discover which opponents they will face as they look to qualify for the third consecutive European Championship under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

Ending a 23-year exile from major tournaments by sealing a spot at Euro 2020 (played in 2021) under former manager Steve Clarke, they repeated the trick three years later, edging out Norway for a spot in the 2024 tournament in Germany.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Now under upcoming boss Pocognoli, a disappointing third-placed finish in the Nations League has made Scotland’s hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - slightly harder after results meant they were placed in Pot 3 of the draw.

Want to know when the draw will take place, how to watch and which teams Scotland could face and which they will avoid? Here is everything you need to know about the Euro 2028 qualifying draw:.

The qualifying draw for the European Championships in 2028 will take place in Belfast, Northern Ireland, on Sunday 6 December 2026. The tournament will be co-hosted by the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.

If you want to stream the draw via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and via the official UEFA YouTube channel.

Sources indicate that scotland’s third-placed finish in Nations League Group B1 means they will be placed into Pot 3 of the draw next month. They will be drawn against once team each from Pots 1, 2 and 4 and potentially pot 5, depending on if they are placed into one of the six five-team groups.

They can’t be drawn against England, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland or Wales, with UEFA keeping the tournament co-hosts separated in the qualifying phase of Euro 2028.

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain.

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkiye.

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

The Euro 2028 qualifiers begin in March 2027, but Scotland’s campaign will depend entirely on the outcome of the qualifying draw in December.

As attested to above, Scotland will be placed into either a four-team or five-team group. If they are drawn in a four team group, fixtures will begin in March 2027. However, should they be drawn in a five team group, their first Euro 2028 qualifying fixture will take place in September 2027.
